node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Leading coefficient of a polynomial
node.description: Identify the leading coefficient of a polynomial written in descending powers.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Descending power order
node.description: Write polynomial terms in descending order of exponent to support comparison and operations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Subtract polynomials with negatives
node.description: Subtract polynomial expressions while distributing the subtraction sign across all terms.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Binomial area model
node.description: Use an area model or grid to expand the product of two binomials.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Perfect square trinomial products
node.description: Recognise and expand products of the form squared binomials that produce perfect square trinomials.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Factor monic quadratics by sum and product
node.description: Factor monic quadratic trinomials by finding two numbers with the required sum and product.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Factor nonmonic quadratics by AC method
node.description: Factor nonmonic quadratic trinomials by using the product of the leading coefficient and constant term to split the middle term.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Difference squares recognition
node.description: Recognise expressions that are differences of two square terms and factor them accordingly.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Zero product property step
node.description: Use the zero-product property to set each factor equal to zero when solving a factorised quadratic equation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Roots from factored form
node.description: Find the roots of a quadratic equation or function from its factored form.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Positive discriminant gives two real roots
node.description: Interpret a positive discriminant as indicating two distinct real roots for a quadratic equation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Zero discriminant gives repeated root
node.description: Interpret a zero discriminant as indicating one repeated real root for a quadratic equation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Negative discriminant gives no real roots
node.description: Interpret a negative discriminant as indicating no real roots for a quadratic equation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Leading coefficient and parabola opening
node.description: Use the sign of the leading coefficient to determine whether a parabola opens upward or downward.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Y intercept from constant term
node.description: Identify the y-intercept of a quadratic function in standard form from the constant term.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Axis of symmetry formula
node.description: Find the axis of symmetry of a quadratic function in standard form using x equals negative b over two a.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vertex from completed square form
node.description: Identify the vertex of a quadratic function from completed-square or vertex form.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Graph quadratic from vertex form
node.description: Sketch a quadratic function from vertex form using the vertex, opening direction and transformations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Graph quadratic from intercepts
node.description: Sketch a quadratic function using its x-intercepts, y-intercept and symmetry.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Choose quadratic solving method
node.description: Choose an efficient method for solving a quadratic equation based on its structure and available information.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Leading term sets polynomial degree
node.description: For a single-variable polynomial in standard order, the leading term determines the degree and leading coefficient.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Zero product sets factors to zero
node.description: If a product equals zero, at least one factor must equal zero, which allows factorised quadratic equations to be solved.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Leading coefficient controls opening direction
node.description: A positive leading coefficient opens a parabola upward, while a negative leading coefficient opens it downward.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Constant term is y intercept in standard form
node.description: In standard form, the constant term gives the y-intercept of the quadratic function.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Axis of symmetry is midpoint of roots
node.description: When two real roots exist, the axis of symmetry lies halfway between their x-values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Subtract only first polynomial term
node.description: Learner subtracts only the first term of a polynomial instead of distributing the subtraction sign to every term.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Zero product used before equation equals zero
node.description: Learner sets factors equal to zero before the quadratic equation has been written in zero-product form.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Discriminant sign cases reversed
node.description: Learner reverses the meaning of positive, zero and negative discriminant cases for real roots.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Constant term is x intercept
node.description: Learner treats the constant term of a quadratic in standard form as an x-intercept instead of the y-intercept.

edge.rationale: Polynomial term analysis includes identifying leading term and leading coefficient.
Area models directly practise expanding binomial products.
Perfect square trinomial products are a core special product pattern.
The positive discriminant case is a core discriminant interpretation.
Opening direction is a core feature of quadratic graphs.
Choosing an efficient solving method is part of strategic quadratic-equation work.
Identifying a leading coefficient requires recognising polynomial terms and coefficients.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify the term with highest exponent or its coefficient.

edge.rationale: Writing in descending order depends on comparing powers and identifying degree.
edge.failure_signal: Learner orders by coefficient size rather than exponent.

edge.rationale: Subtraction of polynomials is a specialised case of adding and subtracting polynomials with sign distribution.
edge.failure_signal: Learner fails to distribute the negative sign across all terms.

edge.rationale: An area model is one representation for expanding binomial products after recognising the binomial product structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot account for all four partial products.

edge.rationale: Perfect-square products are a structured binomial-product case.
edge.failure_signal: Learner omits the middle term or doubles incorrectly.

edge.rationale: Factoring monic quadratics by sum and product requires recognising coefficients in standard form.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses the wrong sum or product from the quadratic expression.

edge.rationale: Nonmonic factorisation extends monic trinomial factorisation patterns.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses b and c only and ignores the leading coefficient.

edge.rationale: Difference-of-squares recognition depends on special product patterns.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies the pattern to a sum of squares or non-square terms.

edge.rationale: Using zero-product solving requires being able to factor a quadratic into linear factors first.
edge.failure_signal: Learner sets factors to zero before moving all terms to one side or before factorising.

edge.rationale: Reading roots from factored form depends on applying the zero-product property to each factor.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives factor values rather than root values.

edge.rationale: Interpreting the positive case depends on understanding the discriminant expression.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot connect the sign of the discriminant with the number of real roots.

edge.rationale: The zero case is a core discriminant interpretation after learning the discriminant.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats a repeated root as two distinct roots or no roots.

edge.rationale: The negative case is a core discriminant interpretation after learning the discriminant.
edge.failure_signal: Learner expects real x-intercepts when the discriminant is negative.

edge.rationale: Reading opening direction from the leading coefficient requires identifying a in standard form.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses the constant term or linear coefficient to decide opening direction.

edge.rationale: Reading the y-intercept from c requires recognising standard form coefficients.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies c as an x-intercept rather than the y-intercept.

edge.rationale: The axis formula uses coefficients from standard form.
edge.failure_signal: Learner substitutes a, b or signs incorrectly in the axis formula.

edge.rationale: Reading the vertex from completed-square form requires recognising that form's parameters.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reverses signs or gives the wrong coordinate order for the vertex.

edge.rationale: Graphing from vertex form depends on interpreting vertex-form transformations.
edge.failure_signal: Learner locates the vertex but cannot apply stretch or reflection features.

edge.rationale: Graphing from intercepts requires finding x-intercepts from factored form or roots.
edge.failure_signal: Learner plots intercepts but cannot use symmetry to sketch the parabola.

edge.rationale: Strategic method choice requires exposure to general formula solving as well as special-case methods.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies the quadratic formula to every case or chooses factorisation when no simple factorisation exists.
